pr_title: SPI: Do not disable SPI peripheral while switching DMA buffers
pr_body:
Removed SPI peripheral disabling when switching DMA to another buffer. When using hardware chip select this would cause to stop driving CS pin when swhitching buffers. This is different (and wrong) than when used software CS.

Fixes #28833

Signed-off-by: Łukasz Mazur <lukasz.mazur@hidglobal.com>

issue_context.title: STM32: SPI DMA Driver - HW CS handling not compatible with spi_nor (Winbond W25Q)
issue_context.body:
**Describe the bug**
When spi_nor driver is sending command over SPI it uses two rx buffers and two tx buffers. In current implementation in function transceive_dma (spi_ll_stm32.c) SPI peripheral is turned off after each buffer finishes resulting in CS pin being pulled up between bytes send. Flash that I use (Winbond W25Q) after falling edge on CS expect command to be send therefore communication does not work. 

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Always reproducible when using spi_nor driver with spi_dma turned on and hardware slave select
CONFIG_SPI_NOR=y
CONFIG_SPI_STM32_USE_HW_SS=y
CONFIG_SPI_STM32_DMA=n

**Expected behavior**
CS not being pulled up when switching DMA for next buffer. This is how it behaves when software CS is used. 

**Impact**
Prevents SPI flash chips form being used with DMA
comments:
> @LuxLuthor what SOC are you using ?

I use STM32WB55RG

> I use STM32WB55RG

Hmm one of the only few STM SOC's I don't have :-/

But I assume the problem happens on all STM32 SOC's, I am not sure if it can be fixed, will have to dive deeper into the DMA/SPI documentation to see how it can be done.

>Impact Prevents SPI flash chips form being used with DMA

You mean not being able to use DMA + HW CS, right ? 

For your use case would using "software" CS be a workaround, or is there a special reason you want/need "hardware" CS support?

I would guess that this is visible on every STM32. Using software CS would be a workaround but I looked into driver code and moved turning SPI peripheral ON and OFF outside while loop that is handling iteration over buffers. It seems to work well now. I will make pull request later today.

> moved turning SPI peripheral ON and OFF outside while loop that is handling iteration over buffers.

We will really have to double check if that doesn't have any side effects, the DMA timing is a bit tricky.  But we can discus that in your PR.

I removed only disabling SPI peripheral. TXDMAEN RXDMAEN stayed in place. Tested on WB55RG with Winbond W25Q and works fine. Enabling/disabling TXDMAEN RXDMAEN while SPI enabled does not seem to be against manual.

review_comments:
Btw, aren't lines 689 to 691 superfluous? (At this stage, cs nor dma are enabled: the transaction has yet to start)

Actually, should these lines be in spi_stm32_init()?
Probably yes but this PR solves only HW CS problem. I don't know what was the idea of the original author.

I think that code ended up there after quit a bit of conversation in the PR that changed that code, I guess nobody had a use case/hardware that used HW CS :-/ I will test (but I won't have time until in the weekend) it on the boards I have, and if those all work I guess it should be OK.

@tbursztyka a quick test shows that line 689 and 690 can be removed, but line 691 `LL_SPI_Disable(spi);` should be changed to `LL_SPI_Enable(spi);` and than line 713 can also be removed. 

So basically enabling spi before the loop and disabling after the loop, and enable/disable DMA in the loop.
nice, can you make a pr?
@LuxLuthor could you add those changes mentioned by me to this PR, or do you want me to make a new combined PR with those changes and your fix ?
@erwango the question was if cleanup the extra enable call in this PR, or if we make two "mini" PR's
@lowlander @LuxLuthor, as long as this is done in 2 commits that are properly documented and current PR description is updated, this can be done here.

@erwango the fix is to remove the disable from the loop, so the enable in the loop makes no sense anymore, and can only be done one time before the loop. so those two changes belong in one (this) commit ? The removing of the dmadisable in front of the loop could be the second commit ?
@erwango @lowlander, Yep, I will add these changes in this PR.
